description:
## Question

Which shells get buck2 moves from 'the shell's toolchain.toml declares buck2' to a per-shell setting in flake.nix next to `turnkey.toolchains.declarationFiles`. What exactly is that setting: its name, type and default (on for every shell? only default?), how it interacts with the global `turnkey.buck2.enable`, and where `turnkey.buck2.version` (read-only) sits? Settle the interface, including what a consumer with a single shell writes.

comments.text:
Resolution:
1. The per-shell setting switches the shell's whole Buck2 integration: binary, prelude, cells, toolchains cell, tk sync hooks and test caching. This is what today's shellNeedsBuck2 gate means.
2. Shape: `turnkey.toolchains.buck2.shells`, a list of shell names, default `[ "default" ]`. Naming a shell missing from `declarationFiles` is an eval error. `declarationFiles` is unchanged.
3. `turnkey.toolchains.buck2.enable` stays the master switch (default false); `shells` applies only when it is on. A single-shell consumer writes `buck2.enable = true;` as today and only deletes buck2-toolchain from toolchain.toml. Turnkey's own docs shell needs no change.
4. `turnkey.toolchains.buck2.version`: read-only str computed from the pinned record, passed to each shell's devenv module as read-only `turnkey.buck2.version`; the welcome message reads it.
5. The standalone devenv module (flake.devenvModules.turnkey) keeps its interface. Its `turnkey.buck2.enable` means this shell gets the pinned buck2 plus the integration, and it resolves the pin itself.

title: What is the shape of the per-shell buck2 option?
